Research Synthesis

The Question

What should AI surface, take off frontline managers' plates, and do on their behalf — proactively, contextually, and within the right boundaries?

Three managers, one consistent posture

Cross-participant convergence on where relief is wanted.

▼

Detail withheld. Cross-participant convergence on where AI relief is wanted, and the specific workflows each manager named as already consuming their time.

Business impact: identifies the lowest-risk entry point for AI adoption, protecting user trust while shortening time to value on the first release. Specific findings withheld.

Short answer: Yes — with clear limits

The scope boundary participants set, and their reasoning.

▼

Detail withheld. The boundary conditions participants placed on AI scope, with the reasoning behind where each drew the line.

Business impact: yields a reusable go/no-go test for AI scope, avoiding build-and-retreat cycles on capability users reject. Specific findings withheld.

Proactivity is wanted — conditionally

How far participants will let a system act on its own.

▼

Detail withheld. Participant-by-participant appetite for proactive system behaviour, and the temperament and team-dynamic factors that explain the variation.

Business impact: locates the boundary where a proactive feature stops aiding retention and begins eroding trust. Specific findings withheld.

Design Principles

Three tests every AI feature must pass

Distilled from three managers across different stacks and industries. Each principle is a go/no-go test applied before any AI feature is scoped.

Principle 1

Automate the plumbing, not the judgment

Where the mandate is unanimous, and where it stops.

▼

Detail withheld. The workflows each participant named as candidates for transactional relief, and the common structure underneath three different expressions of it.

Business impact: a positioning frame that raises perceived value and first-run adoption. Specific findings withheld.

Principle 2

Surface, then send you looking

The form proactive behaviour has to take to be accepted.

▼

Detail withheld. The account that anchors the case for proactive flagging, and the ceiling the same participant placed on how far it should go.

Business impact: keeps proactive capability on the trusted side of the line, protecting adoption across the wider AI suite. Specific findings withheld.

Principle 3

Wall off the human relationship

The relationship boundary participants would not move.

▼

Detail withheld. Where participants drew the line between preparation and mediation, and the reasoning each gave for it.

Business impact: isolates the single failure mode participants said would cause outright abandonment. Specific findings withheld.

Where Enthusiasm Turns Conditional

Trust conditions

Four guardrails separating "I'll use this" from "I don't trust this." They apply to every capability area above, not only the people-data ones.

Cross-cutting pattern across all 3 participants. Not specific to any one stack or role — treat these as universal constraints for this persona.

Guardrail 1 — record integrity

The condition under which trust collapses entirely.

▼

Detail withheld. The trust-collapse condition one participant identified, and what it implies about record integrity.

Business impact: names the integrity requirement that governs whether people-data features can be trusted, audited, and defended. Specific findings withheld.

Guardrail 2 — honest fallibility

What transparency buys, according to one participant.

▼

Detail withheld. One participant's exposure model, and the compensating transparency he asked for in return.

Business impact: reframes a compliance obligation as a trust surface that increases sustained use. Specific findings withheld.

Guardrail 3 — channel protection

A deliberate exclusion, and the value behind it.

▼

Detail withheld. The channel-protection instinct, held by participants who otherwise differ sharply in AI enthusiasm.

Business impact: flags the design choice most likely to drive churn in this segment. Specific findings withheld.

Guardrail 4 — privacy as a gate

The shared hard limit on people-data handling.

▼

Detail withheld. Participant worst-case scenarios for people-data handling, and the shared principle running across all three.

Business impact: establishes a pre-launch gate that avoids rework and regulatory exposure. Specific findings withheld.

Honest Gaps

What this research does not yet answer

Naming gaps is part of responsible synthesis. These are genuine unknowns — not opportunities.

Gap 1 — n=3 is directional, not conclusive

Three managers cannot stand in for the full frontline manager population.

▼

Detail withheld. Three participants across different stacks and industries, with no common organizational AI standard among them. The diligence statement records the limitation explicitly and directs that everything here be read as directional rather than conclusive.

Takeaway: These are strong directional signals. Validate with a broader cohort before making irreversible design decisions.

Gap 2 — a top-ranked ask is single-source

A single-source signal flagged as not yet generalizable.

▼

Detail withheld. A single-source signal, its likely domain-specific explanation, and the reason it is not treated as universal.

Business impact: prevents a single-source signal from being over-weighted into a flagship investment decision. Specific findings withheld.

Gap 3 — a speculative use case lacks corroboration

A speculative use case lacking cross-participant support.

▼

Detail withheld. A use case raised by one participant only, why it appealed to her, and why it lacks cross-participant validation.

Business impact: keeps a speculative finding from being funded at the same confidence as well-supported ones. Specific findings withheld.
